head_commit.message:
chore(v1.00.31-w7): review round 15 returned APPROVED - the wave gate passes

Round 15 ran on the mandated independent route with a shell, executed all seven
mandated checks and all seven re-derivations, found nothing demonstrable, and
returned APPROVED. It is the first round in this wave that did. Fifteen rounds
have now run: fourteen returned CHANGES-REQUESTED and this one approved. The
gate now passes where it reported exactly two rejections an hour ago.

What the fourteen were for is worth stating, because the approval only means
something against what it followed. Rounds 1 to 8 found real defects, mostly in
the evidence rather than the content. Rounds 9 and 10 were the first with a
shell and found prose defects no gate can see, because no gate reads prose.
Rounds 11 and 12 returned CHANGES-REQUESTED for want of evidence rather than for
a defect: they could execute nothing, and said so instead of inferring a
verdict. Round 13 executed everything and found that its own accepted-count had
been retyped by hand one round after being made derived. Round 14 found a wrong
manifest path in my review instruction, and in adjudicating it, that 57 of 63
findings had no recorded disposition at all while the verdict asserted a
four-way partition satisfied by a classifier default.

The content did not change in any of the last four rounds. What changed is that
the review could finally see it and then declined to find anything. The honest
reading is not that fourteen rounds were needed to fix the content - the content
was sound by the ninth - but that the record asserting it took fourteen rounds to
become true, and that the most expensive defect in it, a disposition count the
data never supported, was invisible to every check built to catch it because the
checker and the author were the same mind.

Five claims the approval made false, each corrected at the site that carries it
rather than in the text reporting it. The review report opened by saying every
round returned CHANGES-REQUESTED, said a further round was outstanding, and
declared that the record does not assert approval; all three are corrected, and
the report now carries the counts, because the verdict field is the single token
APPROVED that the gate compares for exact equality and cannot hold prose. The
validation notes made the same two claims and are corrected. The evidence status
becomes the bare token ready-for-merge and the reasoning moves to
merge-authorization.action, which is already the long-form field: a sentence in
status would fail the gate, and a bare token with no reasoning anywhere would
pass it while telling a reader nothing.

The report's figures are interpolated from the findings arrays rather than typed,
and that was not a stylistic choice. I first wrote "15 rounds and 67 findings, of
which 10 carry a status - 8 FIXED" by hand, and the finished-value assertion
caught it in the same pass: round 15 approves and raises nothing, so the total
stays at the round-14 figure. That is the exact defect W7-R13-F1 and W7-R14-F2
are about, committed by the author of the paragraph explaining why not to commit
it. The report now states 15 rounds, 66 findings, 9 statused - 7 FIXED, 1
REFUTED, 1 OPEN - and 57 with no status at all, asserting no disposition for
those, which remains the substance of W7-R14-F2.

Round 15 is recorded with an empty findings list. An approving round that raised
nothing records nothing; inventing a finding to look thorough, or to make the
entry resemble its neighbours, is forbidden.

Two limits on what the approval means, stated by the approving round and recorded
in its not-run register rather than assumed away. The canonical record emitter is
deliberately not in the tree, because it is remediation tooling and committing it
would move the content digest, so its byte-idempotence is not independently
runnable; the reviewer verified the equivalent property, a lossless and
deterministic structural round trip of all three records. And the external
GitHub CI state is not observable from the worktree, so the CI element of the
review is the absence of a contradiction in the record diff, not an observation
of CI. Neither is a defect in the content or the evidence.

Verified after the change: gate PASS with exit 0; 15 rounds with the last
APPROVED and raising nothing; reviewed-sha equal to implementation-sha and both
naming the content head; all three digests agreeing; no duplicate top-level keys
in any record; no duplicated paragraph; no line over 50 KB; each round named
exactly once in the timestamp; no surviving not-approved, outstanding-round or
all-rounds-changes-requested claim in any live field; checksums 14/14, 6/6, 1/1;
provenance 952/950/951; lint-all 23 passed with the same two pre-existing
warnings. Content head 98e582e0 and digest fb4b4332 unchanged.

The merge is authorized on review grounds only. It remains conditional on every
required check being green on the final record head, and the v1.00.31 tag remains
gated on release readiness and the seven-gate tag-publish preflight on clean
main. Nothing in this record authorizes a tag.

Co-Authored-By: coinerd <coinerd@users.noreply.github.com>
